value: 2026-09-10. cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow.py alone: 24 of 24 teeth GREEN in 250.30s at pre-build commit 337eeca6af7b, and 24 of 24 GREEN in 260.62s at HEAD ec7ef37. Charged the 120s default by `cairn test cairn/devices/tester --seal`, the same file wrote `verdict: red` into cairn/devices/tester/validations/test_hollow.json. Same file, same teeth, opposite verdict, and the only thing that changed was the budget. THE SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DEFECT was measured a month earlier and recorded only in a commit message: b62670d found three heavy netns proofs run concurrently pushed past a 900s bound none of them exceeds alone, and `--seal` wrote a red saying the ground loop's beat cannot hold its period - when the beat holds it in 91.3s. The two sites: device.py:514-527 writes RED on TimeoutExpired; cli.py:177-181 prints the same event as neither and writes nothing.

The default budget of 120s is NOT changed by this ticket, and after it ships `cairn test cairn/devices/tester` will still fail to measure test_hollow.py at the default - it will simply say so honestly instead of writing a red. That is the correct resting state and not an oversight: the budget is a tuning question needing a corpus-wide cost distribution nobody has measured, and casting a ticket for work whose input does not exist yet is the hollow shape this system is built against. ALSO INHERITED: the standing red already written into cairn/devices/tester/validations/test_hollow.json by the 2026-09-10 sweep is re-taken green from a solo run under this voyage's sibling ticket 481221f45884, the way b62670d re-took the ground loop's beat. This ticket does not sweep the corpus for older manufactured reds; its watch counts them, which is what turns a backfill into a measured need rather than a guess.

Uncovered by voyage 481221f45884 on 2026-09-10 when its criterion-6 device sweep reported test_hollow.py red at the 120s default. Ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage attaches an uncovered bug to the voyage that found it - it does NOT apply here, and the reason is bounds: 481221f45884 is bounded to how a FIRST SEAL chooses its isolation, and the tester's timeout-to-verdict mapping is a different seam that the sweep merely stood next to. Widening a voyage's bounds is a question for Akien, never a silent act. So this is cast rather than absorbed.
